nodes.label: Siren Camera Infrared Night Frame (2022-02-24 22:00:00)
nodes.description: Monochrome IR still from the '1080P-IPC-Siren' channel at 2022-02-24 22:00:00, same fixed viewpoint as frame00801. Birds are markedly more aggregated here: dense rosettes press around each of the four visible pan feeders and a large clump fills the upper right, while wide stretches of floor in the lower half are empty. The contrast with the 08:53 frame from the same camera makes this a natural pair for studying diurnal redistribution.

nodes.label: Feeder-Centred Clustering Behaviour
nodes.description: The recurring observable behaviour across all six frames: birds form near-circular rosettes radiating outward from each pan feeder, bodies pointing inward toward the pan rim. Rosette thickness (how many concentric rings of birds surround a pan) varies strongly between frames and is the most legible behavioural signal available from the overhead view.
nodes.rationale: Feeder rosette density is a useful proxy for feeding activity precisely because it is measurable without individual tracking — a per-pan radial occupancy count survives the heavy occlusion and low resolution that defeat per-bird identity tracking in a densely stocked house.

nodes.label: Resting / Sitting Distribution on Open Floor
nodes.description: Away from the feeder line, birds appear as motionless rounded blobs with tucked outlines rather than the elongated shape of a walking bird, and they are distributed in loose patches with bare floor between them. Distinguishing this resting state from feeding is the second behavioural class the overhead footage can support.
